claims.text: Adding approximately 0.5 at% yttrium to a refractory high-entropy alloy will enhance its radiation tolerance.
Yttrium addition will promote the formation of stable nanoscale oxide or nitride precipitates.
Yttrium-derived oxide or nitride precipitates will act as sinks for irradiation-induced defects.
The proposed precipitates will capture and recombine radiation-induced point defects.
Defect capture and recombination at the precipitates will reduce radiation-induced defect accumulation and microstructural damage.
Fine yttrium-derived precipitates will form in situ during alloy processing.
The yttrium-induced microstructural changes will not adversely affect the alloy's load-bearing characteristics.
The yttrium-added alloy will exhibit a lower post-irradiation defect density, including fewer dislocation loops or voids, than the unmodified alloy.
The yttrium-added alloy will retain yield strength and other mechanical properties better than the unmodified alloy under identical irradiation conditions.
The beneficial effect is expected under irradiation at approximately 500°C to 800°C that simulates high-energy particle exposure in fusion plasma-facing environments.
The beneficial effect is expected specifically at a low yttrium concentration around 0.5 at%.
Departures from the proposed yttrium concentration or exposure to extreme conditions may alter phase stability or mechanical performance.
Preliminary evidence supports the role of yttrium-induced precipitates in defect mitigation.
The exact quantitative improvement and long-term precipitate stability under prolonged irradiation remain undetermined.
